rule_or_pattern: Typewritten district codes: a leading token made only of Ι/I/Ο/O letters followed by '.' is a number -> map Ι/I->1, Ο/O->0 (regex ^([ΙIΟO]{2,4})\. ; e.g. 'ΙΙΙ.'->'111.', 'ΙΟΙ.'->'101.'). Also fix the leading '–' that the print shows as '=': ^(\d+ )?– -> '\1= '. Alternatively drop lines matching ^[ΙIΟO]{2,4}\. and ^(\d+ )?– .
notes: This is a 35-line typewritten table of Greek electoral districts (all-caps headings explain the flags), and most labels match the typescript: 1, 3, 4, 6-11, 13-20, 22-35. The typewriter '1' looks like 'I', so the numeric codes '111.' (2) and '101.' (5) are labelled as the letters 'ΙΙΙ.' and 'ΙΟΙ.', while the same codes elsewhere (102., 103., 107.) are read as digits. The '=' after the item number is read as '–' in 12 and 21. Breathings typed as separate marks ('῾Αγ.', '᾿Ασπροχώματος') are handled by the pool rule.
